models.name: discussion_board_guests
models.description: Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for anonymous browsing access. Guest actors can view sections, articles, comments, and search content without full authentication. Each guest is uniquely identified by their device fingerprint for session continuity across requests. This table serves as the root identity record for guest actors, with sessions tracked in discussion_board_guest_sessions.

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique device fingerprint identifying the guest user across sessions. Generated from device characteristics for anonymous identification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted. Null indicates active account.

models.name: discussion_board_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access with device-based identification. This table tracks all active sessions for guest users, storing connection metadata including IP address, page href, and referrer information for security auditing and session management. Sessions are append-only records that expire based on the expired_at timestamp.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link discussion_board_guests} via discussion_board_guest_id
- One guest can have multiple sessions (1:N relationship)
- Sessions are managed through authentication flows, not direct user CRUD operations

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Guest account this session belongs to. {@link discussion_board_guests.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address for the session connection. Used for security auditing and session validation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current page URL (href) when session was created. Tracks user navigation context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to session creation. Used for analytics and security tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp. Records when the guest logged in or accessed the system.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp. Sessions are invalidated after this time for security purposes. NOT NULL to ensure all sessions have defined lifecycles.

models.name: discussion_board_members
models.description: Registered member accounts with email/password authentication credentials and profile information. Members can create articles, write comments, and request administrator access. This table serves as the primary identity record for member actors, with sessions tracked separately in discussion_board_member_sessions. Ban status is tracked here to control login and content access permissions.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address for authentication and account identification. Must be unique across all member accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hashed password for secure authentication. Never stored or transmitted in plaintext.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown on articles, comments, and user profiles. Used to identify the member in the discussion board.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional user biography or profile description. Provides additional context about the member to other users.

plainFields.name: ban_status
plainFields.description: Current ban status controlling login and content access. Values: 'active' (normal access), 'banned' (login blocked). Updated via discussion_board_ban_records.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for ban if ban_status is 'banned'. Set by administrator when creating ban record in discussion_board_ban_records.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp. Records when the member registered.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last profile update timestamp. Updated on display_name, bio, or ban status changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for account removal. When set, account is logically deleted but data preserved for audit.

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table tracks login sessions for discussion_board_members, storing connection context including IP address, page href, and referrer for security auditing. Each member can have multiple concurrent sessions, and sessions are managed through authentication flows rather than direct user CRUD operations.

Sessions are append-only audit trails that record when members log in and when their sessions expire. The expired_at field is mandatory (NOT NULL) to enforce session timeout policies and prevent indefinite access.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussion_board_members.id} that owns this session.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Page href where login occurred for connection context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL for connection context and analytics.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Session last update timestamp for audit trail.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp. NOT NULL by default for security to enforce session timeout.

models.name: discussion_board_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for member account recovery with expiration timestamps. This table stores one-time use tokens that members receive via email to reset their passwords. Each token has a limited validity period and is invalidated after use.

Relationships: Belongs to {@link discussion_board_members} via discussion_board_member_id. A member can have multiple password reset requests over time, but only one active reset token at a time.

Usage Pattern: When a member requests a password reset, a new token is generated with an expiration time. The token is sent via email and can be used once to reset the password. After use or expiration, the token becomes invalid.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Target member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. The member requesting the password reset.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token. This is a cryptographically secure random string sent to the member's email for account recovery.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp. Password reset tokens are valid only until this time and become invalid after expiration.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was used for password reset. Null if the token has not been used yet. After use, the token is invalidated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp. When the password reset request was initiated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp. Updated when token is used or status changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Marks the record as deleted while preserving audit trail.

models.name: discussion_board_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for member registration confirmation. Stores temporary tokens sent to member email addresses during registration process, tracking expiration and verification status for account activation workflow.

This table supports the member registration authentication flow by maintaining verification tokens that must be validated before account activation. Tokens expire after a configured duration and are marked as verified upon successful confirmation.

Related entities:
- {@link discussion_board_members}: Parent member account that requested verification
- {@link discussion_board_member_sessions}: Session created after successful email verification

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member account requesting email verification. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure verification token sent to member email address.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp. Token becomes invalid after this time.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when email verification was successfully completed. Null if not yet verified.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit trail.

models.name: discussion_board_admins
models.description: Administrator accounts with email/password authentication and elevated privilege levels. This table represents the primary identity record for administrators who manage sections, moderate content, ban/unban users, and review administrator requests. Each administrator has one-to-many sessions stored in {@link discussion_board_admin_sessions}, password reset tokens in {@link discussion_board_admin_password_resets}, and audit logs in {@link discussion_board_admin_audit_logs}.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator's unique email address for authentication and communication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt hashed password for secure authentication.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown to users in the discussion board.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biography or description of the administrator.

plainFields.name: grade
plainFields.description: Administrator grade level: 'regular' for standard admins, 'super' for super administrators who can manage other administrators.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was soft-deleted. Null if account is active.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for administrator authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table tracks all login sessions for {@link discussion_board_admins} administrators, storing connection metadata including IP address, page reference, and referrer information for security auditing and session management. Each session record represents a single authenticated session with expiration tracking for automatic logout enforcement.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to exactly one {@link discussion_board_admins} administrator account
- Many sessions per administrator (1:N relationship)
- Append-only audit trail of login events

Behavioral notes:
- Sessions are managed through authentication flows, not direct user CRUD
- Expired sessions should be periodically cleaned up
- Connection context enables security monitoring and anomaly detection

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator's {@link discussion_board_admins.id} who owns this session.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address for connection tracking and security auditing.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current page URL (href) where authentication occurred.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating the page that led to authentication.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp marking when the administrator logged in.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp for automatic logout enforcement. NOT NULL by default for security.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrator account recovery with expiration timestamps.

This table stores one-time use tokens generated when administrators request password resets. Each token is associated with a specific admin account and has a limited validity period for security purposes. After successful password reset or expiration, tokens are soft-deleted.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link discussion_board_admins} through discussion_board_admin_id
- Tokens are single-use and expire automatically

Security notes:
- Tokens should be cryptographically secure random strings
- Tokens expire after a short period (e.g., 1 hour)
- Old tokens are invalidated when new ones are generated

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator account requesting password reset. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure random token for password reset verification.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp. Tokens become invalid after this time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Token creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Token last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for token cleanup.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_audit_logs
models.description:
Audit trail recording all administrator actions for security and compliance tracking. This table captures immutable records of administrative operations including article/comment CRUD, user bans/unbans, section management, and admin request approvals. Each record references the acting administrator, action type, affected resource, and timestamp for accountability and forensic analysis. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

Use cases:
- Security audit trails for compliance requirements
- Forensic analysis of administrative actions
- Accountability tracking for moderator actions
- System monitoring and anomaly detection

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the action. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed (e.g., ARTICLE_CREATE, ARTICLE_DELETE, USER_BAN, SECTION_UPDATE, ADMIN_REQUEST_APPROVE).

plainFields.name: resource_type
plainFields.description: Type of resource affected by the action (e.g., article, comment, section, user, admin_request, ban_record).

plainFields.name: resource_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the affected resource. Nullable for actions without specific resource target.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the action performed with business context.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the action was performed for security tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit record was soft-deleted. Audit records are typically never deleted for compliance.

models.name: discussion_board_audit_logs
models.description:
Immutable audit trail recording all system actions including article/comment CRUD operations, user bans/unbans, section management, and admin request approvals.

This table serves as a centralized compliance and accountability mechanism, tracking every significant action performed across the platform. Each record captures the actor who performed the action, the action type, the affected resource, and contextual metadata.

Key relationships:
- References {@link discussion_board_members} for member actions
- References {@link discussion_board_admins} for administrator actions
- References various resources through polymorphic resource_type and resource_id fields

Behavioral notes:
- Append-only: Records are never modified or deleted
- No soft delete: deleted_at is always null for audit integrity
- Polymorphic references: Uses resource_type + resource_id to track different entity types
- Actor tracking: Uses member_id or admin_id based on actor type performing the action

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who performed the action, if applicable. References {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Null for admin actions or system-triggered events.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the action, if applicable. References {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. Null for member actions or system-triggered events.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who performed the action: 'member' for registered users, 'admin' for administrators, 'system' for automated processes.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Specific action performed. Values: 'article.create', 'article.update', 'article.delete', 'comment.create', 'comment.update', 'comment.delete', 'section.create', 'section.update', 'section.delete', 'user.ban', 'user.unban', 'admin_request.submit', 'admin_request.approve', 'admin_request.reject', 'file.upload', 'file.delete', 'image.upload', 'image.delete'.

plainFields.name: resource_type
plainFields.description: Type of resource affected by the action: 'article', 'comment', 'section', 'user', 'admin_request', 'file_attachment', 'image_attachment'. Used with resource_id for polymorphic reference.

plainFields.name: resource_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the affected resource. Combined with resource_type for polymorphic reference to {@link discussion_board_articles.id}, {@link discussion_board_comments.id}, {@link discussion_board_sections.id}, etc.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Optional JSON string containing additional context about the action (e.g., ban reason, old/new values for updates, request details). Stored as string to maintain database portability.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address of the client that performed the action. Used for security auditing and abuse detection.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string from the client request. Used for device/browser identification in audit trails.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action occurred. Immutable once set.

models.name: discussion_board_system_settings
models.description: System-wide configuration settings for platform parameters, feature flags, and operational thresholds accessible across all domains. Stores key-value pairs with audit trail for centralized system configuration management.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique setting identifier used to reference this configuration value across the system.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: The configuration value for this setting. Format depends on the setting type (boolean, number, string, JSON).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable description explaining the purpose and valid values of this setting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system setting was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system setting was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this system setting was soft-deleted. Null if the setting is active.

models.name: discussion_board_sections
models.description: Discussion board sections organizing articles into topic categories with administrator-managed lifecycle states. Each section represents a distinct topic area (e.g., Politics, Economy, Current Affairs) and serves as the primary organizational structure for content browsing and filtering. Sections are created and managed exclusively by administrators, while all actors can browse and view articles within sections. {@link discussion_board_articles} belong to sections through a many-to-one relationship, and {@link discussion_board_admins} create and maintain sections.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who created this section. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique section name identifying the topic category (e.g., 'Politics', 'Economy', 'Technology'). Used for URL slugs and display purposes.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining the section's topic focus and content guidelines.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was soft-deleted. Null indicates active section.

models.name: discussion_board_section_snapshots
models.description: Point-in-time snapshots of section data for audit trail and historical tracking. Captures denormalized section states at specific moments to enable historical reconstruction and compliance auditing. Each snapshot is immutable and append-only, recording the complete state of a {@link discussion_board_sections} entity at the time of capture.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced section's {@link discussion_board_sections.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Section name denormalized from parent entity.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Section description denormalized from parent entity.

plainFields.name: section_created_at
plainFields.description: Original section creation timestamp denormalized from parent entity.

plainFields.name: section_updated_at
plainFields.description: Original section last update timestamp denormalized from parent entity.

plainFields.name: section_deleted_at
plainFields.description: Original section soft-delete timestamp denormalized from parent entity.

plainFields.name: captured_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was captured.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description: Core article entities representing user-generated content with title, body text, and metadata. Each article belongs to exactly one section for categorization and is owned by one member who has full control over editing and deletion. Articles support soft deletion to preserve content history while removing them from public views. The article body and title are indexed for full-text search capabilities, enabling users to discover content through keyword matching. Article attachments (files and images) are managed through separate junction tables to maintain normalization principles. Comment counts are computed dynamically rather than stored to ensure data consistency.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Section that categorizes this article. {@link discussion_board_sections.id}. Articles must belong to exactly one section for organizational purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who owns and authored this article. {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Only the owner can edit or delete the article, unless an administrator performs moderation actions.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title displayed in lists and article pages. Required for article creation with maximum character limit enforcement for display purposes. Used for search indexing.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main content text of the article. Required for article creation with minimum and maximum character length validation. Used for search indexing.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was originally published. Preserved throughout article lifecycle and editing operations.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was last modified. Updated whenever title, body, or metadata changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was soft-deleted. When null, article is visible; when set, article is hidden from lists but preserved for audit purposes. Administrators can permanently remove articles.

models.name: discussion_board_tags
models.description:
Tag definitions for article categorization and search. Tags are reusable across multiple articles enabling flexible content organization and filtering. Each tag has a unique name and optional description for context.

Tags support:
- Article categorization through M:N relationship with {@link discussion_board_articles}
- Search and filtering across articles
- Independent tag management and discovery

See {@link discussion_board_article_tags} for the junction table linking tags to articles.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique tag name used for article categorization and search filtering.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description providing context about the tag's purpose and usage.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was soft-deleted for archival purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_article_tags
models.description:
Junction table linking articles to tags in a many-to-many relationship for flexible categorization and search.

This table enables articles to have multiple tags and tags to be associated with multiple articles. Each row represents a single article-tag association, allowing for efficient filtering and browsing by tag categories.

Key relationships:
- References {@link discussion_board_articles.id} for article ownership
- References {@link discussion_board_tags.id} for tag categorization
- Composite unique constraint prevents duplicate article-tag associations

Business behavior:
- Created when tags are assigned to articles during creation or editing
- Deleted when tags are removed from articles or when articles are deleted (cascade)
- Supports efficient tag-based article queries and tag popularity calculations

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_tag_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced tag's {@link discussion_board_tags.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp for modification tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for logical removal while preserving historical data.

models.name: discussion_board_article_snapshots
models.description: Point-in-time snapshots of articles capturing historical states for audit trail and version history tracking. Each snapshot records the complete article data at a specific moment, enabling reconstruction of article states over time and compliance with data retention policies. Snapshots are created automatically when articles are created, updated, or deleted to preserve immutable historical records. References {@link discussion_board_articles} for the current article state and {@link discussion_board_members} for article ownership.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Target article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Links this snapshot to its parent article for historical tracking.

plainFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
plainFields.description: Section identifier where the article was categorized at snapshot time. Denormalized from {@link discussion_board_sections.id} for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
plainFields.description: Article owner's member identifier at snapshot time. Denormalized from {@link discussion_board_members.id} for ownership audit trail.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title captured at snapshot time. Preserves historical title even if article is later edited.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Article body content captured at snapshot time. Preserves historical content for version comparison and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: tags
plainFields.description: Comma-separated tag list at snapshot time. Preserves historical categorization for search and filtering audit trails.

plainFields.name: file_count
plainFields.description: Number of file attachments at snapshot time. Tracks attachment history for storage audit.

plainFields.name: image_count
plainFields.description: Number of image attachments at snapshot time. Tracks image history for storage audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Snapshot creation timestamp. Records when this historical state was captured.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the snapshot record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for snapshot records. Allows archival while preserving audit trail.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Single-level comments on articles with author attribution and article references. Each comment belongs to exactly one article and one member, supporting independent editing and deletion by owners. Comments enable article discussion without threading capabilities.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link discussion_board_articles} via discussion_board_article_id (1:N relationship)
- Written by {@link discussion_board_members} via discussion_board_member_id (1:N relationship)

Behavioral notes:
- Article deletion cascades to all associated comments
- Owners can edit and delete their own comments
- Administrators can delete any comment for moderation
- Soft deletion via deleted_at field preserves audit trail
- Chronological display ordered by created_at (oldest first)

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Comment belongs to this article.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Author member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Comment written by this member.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Comment text content. The actual message or response written by the member.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was initially created. Used for chronological ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last modified. Updated on each edit operation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was soft-deleted. Null if comment is active. Preserves audit trail while hiding from normal queries.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of comments for audit trail and historical tracking. Captures comment state at the time of edits or deletions, enabling review of comment modification history and accountability. Each snapshot is immutable once created and references its parent {@link discussion_board_comments}.

Snapshots are automatically created when:
- A comment is edited (captures previous state)
- A comment is deleted (captures state before deletion)

This table supports audit requirements and enables administrators to review comment modification history for moderation purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment's {@link discussion_board_comments.id}. Each snapshot belongs to exactly one comment.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Comment content at the time of snapshot. Denormalized from parent comment for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
plainFields.description: Article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id} that the comment belonged to. Denormalized for efficient querying without joining parent comment.

plainFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
plainFields.description: Member's {@link discussion_board_members.id} who authored the comment. Denormalized for efficient querying without joining parent comment.

plainFields.name: comment_created_at
plainFields.description: Original comment creation timestamp. Denormalized from parent comment for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: comment_updated_at
plainFields.description: Comment's last update timestamp at the time of snapshot. Denormalized from parent comment.

plainFields.name: snapshot_created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Records the exact moment the comment state was captured.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_requests
models.description:
Administrator privilege requests submitted by members for super administrator review. Members request admin status with justification reasons, and super administrators review/approve/reject these requests. Tracks request lifecycle from submission through final decision with accountability timestamps.

Key relationships:
- {@link discussion_board_members.id}: The member who submitted the request
- {@link discussion_board_admins.id}: The super administrator who reviewed the request (null until reviewed)

Status workflow: pending → approved/rejected (terminal states)

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Submitting member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. The member requesting administrator privileges.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewing super administrator's {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. Null until request is reviewed.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Member's justification for requesting administrator privileges. Explains why they believe they should have admin access.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Request status in workflow. Values: 'pending' (awaiting review), 'approved' (granted admin status), 'rejected' (denied). Terminal states: approved, rejected.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when member submitted the administrator request.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when super administrator reviewed and made decision on the request. Null if still pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for administrative archival.

models.name: discussion_board_ban_records
models.description:
User ban records with moderation accountability and audit trail.

This table tracks all user ban actions taken by administrators, including the reason for banning, timestamp, and the administrator who performed the action. Ban records enable:

- Login restriction enforcement for banned users
- Ban reason recording and visibility to administrators
- User unbanning process with audit history
- Banned user list management and review
- Ban accountability through administrator attribution

Each ban record references {@link discussion_board_members.id} for the banned user and {@link discussion_board_admins.id} for the administrator who created the ban. When a user is unbanned, the unbanned_at timestamp is recorded but the ban record remains for historical audit purposes.

Related entities: {@link discussion_board_members}, {@link discussion_board_admins}, {@link discussion_board_audit_logs}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Banned user's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. This reference enables login restriction enforcement and content visibility rules for banned accounts.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who created the ban's {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. Provides accountability and audit trail for moderation actions.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for banning the user. Required field documenting the moderation decision and violation details.

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user was banned. Used for enforcing login restrictions and calculating ban duration.

plainFields.name: unbanned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user was unbanned. Nullable to track active vs historical bans. When set, login restrictions are lifted but record remains for audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp for audit trail and ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp for tracking modifications.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Ban records are typically retained permanently for audit purposes but may be soft-deleted for data management.
